reason: Both sell networking hardware plus software and services to B2B and government buyers, but the products and core customers differ. Digi sells IoT connectivity devices (cellular and rail routers, console servers, modules) and device-management cloud to enterprises, OEMs, transit and smart-city buyers. Ribbon sells session border controllers, IP routing, optical transport and voice core software, mostly to telecom carriers. The overlap is in routing and network management, not in the same product for the same buyer.
